# Correctness lens checkpoint

## Status: in progress

## Files read so far: none

## Next: read cycle-orchestrator.sh around line 2579, router-rc-classify.sh, spec-coverage plugin, spec-correspondence plugin, review-report plugin

findings.message: mktemp is called unconditionally on every spec_coverage_run invocation — including the success path — adding one temp-file creation, a file write, a cat read, and an rm per stage run, even though the rc-file is only needed when route_to_model exits non-zero.

mktemp is called unconditionally at the top of spec_correspondence_run — including when n==0 (no SPECs to check) — so a temp file is created, initialized, and then cleaned up without ever being written by _sc_call; deferring the allocation to the non-zero-n branch or to the rc-classification block would avoid the process spawn on the vacuous path.

The same `_sc_rc_file` is passed to both the batch call (line 253) and each individual per-spec fallback call (line 273); the last `printf '%s' "$?"` written by any call overwrites earlier writes, so if the batch times out (rc=124) but one subsequent individual fallback call succeeds (rc=0), `_sc_router_rc` is read as 0 and `_sc_disposition` is reported as 'complete' — masking the batch timeout and preventing `_route_escalate_timeout` from growing the budget on the next retry cycle; the test covers only the all-calls-fail scenario.

When `mktemp` fails and `_scv_rc_file` is empty, the inner subshell executes `printf '%s' "$?" > ""` which generates a bash error on stderr (suppressed by `|| true`) but silently abandons the rc capture, causing `_rtm_rc` to remain 0 and the disposition to stay 'complete' even when `route_to_model` times out; `spec-correspondence` avoids this with the safer `${_rc_file:-/dev/null}` pattern but `spec-coverage` does not apply the same guard.

Several sentences in the background narrative were rewritten from present to past tense (e.g. 'has ever emitted' → 'emitted', 'has never run' → 'never ran') as editorial cleanup; §C requires updating the status, vocabulary, and §1/§4 prescription text, but does not ask for prose tense changes elsewhere in the document — minor additional edits within an in-scope file.

mktemp creates a world-accessible path in /tmp; a local attacker who replaces the file between the subshell write (printf '$?' > ...) and the parent-shell read (cat) could substitute an arbitrary integer, causing the wrong disposition word to be emitted — at worst 'complete' instead of 'timed_out', which re-introduces the false-convergence defect this change exists to prevent.

Same mktemp-in-/tmp pattern as spec-coverage: a local attacker could overwrite the rc file between the inner-subshell write and the outer read, controlling which disposition word is written to spec-correspondence-result.json.

A single `_sc_rc_file` is shared across the batch call and every per-spec fallback call; if the batch call times out (rc=124) but a subsequent per-spec fallback call succeeds (rc=0), the final `_sc_router_rc` reads 0 and `disposition: complete` is written — the timeout signal is silently lost.

`_scv_rc_file` is created with `mktemp` but no trap is installed; if `spec_coverage_run` exits unexpectedly between the `mktemp` call and the `rm -f` at line 192, the temp file leaks — the same pattern applies to `_sc_rc_file` in `spec-correspondence/plugin.sh`.

When a lens `.rc` file is absent (lens subshell died before writing it), the `|| echo 1` fallback produces rc=1 which `router_reason_disposition` maps to the catch-all `unavailable`; a lens killed by a signal would be classified as `unavailable` rather than `interrupted`, misrepresenting the failure cause in the disposition field.

`cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence` emits only `iter` and `reason=member_did_not_finish`; unlike `cycle.build_unfinished.suppressed_convergence` which also emits `build_verdict`, this event carries no member identity — determining which member triggered suppression requires separately cross-referencing the verdicts blob.

Before this change `review-report` always wrote `disposition: complete` on lens failure; after, it writes `disposition: unavailable` (rc=1) or `timed_out` (rc=124). `unavailable` is NOT in `disposition_unfinished`, so the new cycle suppression does not fire for it — but any engine consumer that applies the ADR-054 §6 response table to this field will now see `halt_unavailable` where it previously saw `proceed`, a net-new halt path for this advisory stage.
